scope: Independent photographic and rendered-image surface review only. This agent did not operate UE or change project assets. Only this research report was written.
status: Visual improvement accepted with fidelity and registration limits; not a measured reconstruction certification.

sources.observed: Pale alternating-direction short rectangular mosaic on lower walls and columns, narrow dark tiled cap, dark speckled skirting, pale terrazzo with dark/light irregular aggregate, thin slab joints and broad dark speckled floor bands. A reflective panel zone is on the right side when looking toward the cross wall.
sources.limits: Wet muddy cleanup state changes floor colour and reflectance. Furniture is being moved. Neither calibrated dimensions nor normal seating layout can be read from this photo.

sources.observed: Dry-looking pale warm-grey/beige terrazzo with distinct dark and pale aggregate, subtle slab joints and a broad black speckled band; matching cross/window wall and pale basket-pattern mosaic column.
sources.limits: Publication year is not a confirmed capture date. The small image and people obscure layout. Use for dry material character, not surveyed values.

sources.observed: Reflective side panels and the blue hanging recycling sign are consistent with the HK01 room view.
sources.limits: 290 by 202 pixels; no reliable panel endpoint or panel material measurement.

sources.observed: Reverse dining view includes reflective panels at image left, white beams, tables and tall side windows.
sources.limits: 376 by 282 pixels with people obscuring room edges. Does not locate the panel zone on the model.

before_review.C27: Whole view reads warmer and more beige/brown than the references. The mosaic becomes nearly uniform at this distance; the floor reads as fine fairly uniform sand rather than strongly separated terrazzo aggregate.
before_review.C24_correction_to_initial_impression: The close render and shader source confirm that the existing pattern already is alternating short rectangular basket mosaic. It should not be replaced with a new square-tile scheme. Weak middle-distance visibility is not evidence that the physical module must be enlarged.
before_review.photometric_limit: Uncalibrated camera exposure, lighting, white balance, viewing distance and pixel density differ. This is a directional visual comparison, not sampled true albedo, measured grain size, or a numerical fidelity score.

implemented_revision_as_reported_by_pare.dimension_status: Existing editable visual estimates retained, not measured real tile dimensions or confirmed strip count.
implemented_revision_as_reported_by_pare.shader_changes: Separate near grout/detail filtering from middle-distance block-average colour; small grout-contrast and normal changes.
implemented_revision_as_reported_by_pare.floor_changes: Aggregate scale multiplied by 1.2, stronger light/dark separation and less yellow matrix; polished-flat surface without gravel displacement.
implemented_revision_as_reported_by_pare.lighting_changes: 21 dining lights changed from 5300 K to 6000 K with intensity unchanged.
implemented_revision_as_reported_by_pare.lighting_status: Rendering choice to produce a more neutral appearance, not confirmation of installed real lamp colour temperature.
implemented_revision_as_reported_by_pare.verification_scope: Implementation details above were relayed by parent. This agent verified rendered appearance only, not live asset settings or shader compilation.

C28.improvement: Compared with matching C27 framing, lower-wall material retains visible small-scale variation instead of becoming an almost plain field. Floor and wall appear less yellow, and visible foreground floor aggregate has more useful dark/light separation.
C28.excluded_from_review: Lower-right desktop thumbnail popup is UI, not scene geometry or material. Clean recapture is appropriate for delivery.

C29.improvement: Short rectangular basket pattern and shallow joints are legible. The skirting reads as a black matrix containing pale aggregate. The floor has varied irregular dark/light chips and still reads as a smooth terrazzo surface.
C29.major_visible_defects: No obvious gross stretching, protruding gravel relief, broken window-edge finish, or severe pattern distortion in this static view.
C29.minor_watch_item: Pink and cream block-to-block contrast is somewhat more conspicuous than the pale real-photo wall, producing a mild patchwork/checker impression. Different exposure and close viewing prevent calling the amplitude definitively wrong. Keep this revision rather than further enlarging modules or substantially increasing colour contrast; reduce block variation slightly only if a matched-view review still finds it too strong.
C29.limits: A still image cannot verify temporal shimmer, mip transitions while walking, performance or collisions. Exact dimensions, phase, chip distribution and roughness remain appearance estimates.

after_review.recommendation: Accept the visible improvement for this pass. Keep natural dry terrazzo reflection and restrained wall relief. Do not copy muddy flood-water gloss or turn grout into deep grooves.

black_trim_and_floor_joint_decisions.cap: References support a narrow dark tiled cap, with small individual joint breaks. Preserve the currently accepted cap path; no photograph-derived new height is asserted.
black_trim_and_floor_joint_decisions.skirting: References support dark speckled terrazzo-like skirting, not an entirely featureless black painted strip. C29 now conveys this material distinction. Do not infer a new perimeter height from these uncalibrated images.
black_trim_and_floor_joint_decisions.floor_bands: Broad black speckled floor bands are a real missing feature, but their complete coordinates, widths and junctions remain unsolved. The cross anchor supplies room direction and one location, not a unique calibrated floor mapping. No invented full-room band grid is recommended.
black_trim_and_floor_joint_decisions.floor_joints: Fine joints are visible within pale terrazzo. Their existence is supported, but slab spacing, origin and complete course alignment are not measured. Do not represent a guessed exact room-wide joint grid as verified.

reflective_wall_registration.direction_now_supported: Relative to facing the user-confirmed cross/window wall, the reflective surface is on the right-hand adjacent side. Under the parent's current campus convention, this is the v=30.4 side direction.
reflective_wall_registration.new_cross_anchor_effect: The confirmed cross position helps establish handedness and room orientation. It does not supply panel endpoints, length, height, or a photo-to-world scale for the right wall.
reflective_wall_registration.material_identity: The photographs show reflection and panel divisions; they do not decisively distinguish mirror glass from polished metal or other reflective cladding. Do not label it a confirmed glass mirror or a roller shutter.
remaining_unknowns: Where the reflective panel run begins and ends along the wall
Whether the panel zone reaches the cross-wall corner or is separated by painted/tiled wall and openings
Relationship to the user-plan doors, shop and washbasin
Whether all images show the same refurbishment state
reflective_wall_registration.safe_action: Retain research evidence and right-side directional annotation only. Do not add a full-width reflective wall or locate individual panels using the cross anchor alone.
